atoms.name: Race conditions and atomicity
atoms.one_line: Shared data plus a non-atomic read-modify-write (load, add, store) makes the result depend on the interleaving.

atoms.name: Critical-section requirements
atoms.one_line: Mutual exclusion, progress (outsiders must not block entry) and bounded waiting, with no assumption about speeds.

atoms.name: Software solutions: turn, flags, Peterson
atoms.one_line: Strict alternation breaks progress; flag-only can deadlock; Peterson (flag[i]=true; turn=j; wait while flag[j] and turn==j) meets all three.

atoms.name: Hardware atomics and spin locks
atoms.one_line: Test-and-set, swap and fetch-and-add give mutual exclusion by busy waiting; bounded waiting is not guaranteed.

atoms.name: Semaphores: wait, signal, values
atoms.one_line: wait decrements and blocks when the value goes below 0; signal increments and wakes one; binary mutex starts at 1, counting starts at the permit count.

atoms.name: Ordering with semaphores
atoms.one_line: A semaphore initialised to 0 makes one thread wait for another; a chain of them fixes the print order; a barrier counts arrivals.

atoms.name: Producer-consumer
atoms.one_line: empty = N, full = 0, mutex = 1; wait the counting semaphore first, then the mutex; the other order can deadlock.

atoms.name: Readers-writers
atoms.one_line: Readers share, writers exclude everyone; first reader locks wrt, last reader unlocks it, readcount needs its own mutex; reader preference can starve writers.

atoms.name: Possible values and outputs of concurrent code
atoms.one_line: Respect program order and semaphore blocking, then enumerate interleavings; a lost update loses a write, never invents one.

patterns.name: Possible outputs or final values of concurrent threads
